verdict: SoundHound's revenue jumped 48% to a record $62M after closing the LivePerson deal, and a $23M paper gain on deal liabilities helped cut its net loss to $46M.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: Up 48% from $42M a year ago — a record quarter

kpis.label: 2026 revenue guidance
kpis.note: Full-year guide; 2027 guided to $350–400M, with sustained adjusted EBITDA profit expected in the second half of 2027

segments.name: Voice and agentic AI
segments.note: All of SoundHound's revenue: voice and conversational AI for cars, restaurants, customer care and enterprises, now including LivePerson (bought September 4). The company reports as a single segment, so there is no official split to show.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin, swollen by buying and combining six businesses, most recently LivePerson. Up 48% YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the voice and agentic AI platform (OASYS). Up 35% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling to carmakers, restaurant chains and enterprises. Up 11% YoY.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: The accounting cost of spreading past acquisitions' technology and customer relationships over their useful lives — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: Earn-out fair-value gain
opex.note: A gain, not a cost: the paper value of earn-out shares owed to sellers of acquired companies fell with the share price, so this line reduced operating costs by $23.4M. It was a $66.2M charge a year ago.

otherDetail: Other expense was just $0.2M, net: $0.2M of other expense and a small amount of interest expense. The tax line was a $0.4M benefit, which added slightly to the bottom line.

takeaways.title: Record revenue, bigger company
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 48% to $62.4M, a record, helped by closing the LivePerson acquisition on September 4. GAAP gross margin fell to 34% from 43% a year ago as lower-margin acquired businesses joined and some upfront licence deals shift to hosted models; on the company's non-GAAP basis gross margin was 50%.

takeaways.title: A paper gain flattered the loss
takeaways.text: Operating costs include a $23.4M gain from revaluing earn-out liabilities (shares owed to sellers of bought companies, re-priced each quarter with the stock). A year ago the same line was a $66.2M charge. Leaving it out, the operating loss would have been about $70M, not $46M.

takeaways.title: Still loss-making, with a dated target
takeaways.text: The net loss narrowed to $46.4M from $109.3M a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA (the company's cash-style profit measure) was a $20.7M loss. SoundHound guided 2026 revenue to $250–260M and 2027 to $350–400M, and says it expects sustained adjusted EBITDA profit in the second half of 2027, helped by $120M of identified annual cost savings.

oneTimers: The $23.4M gain on contingent acquisition liabilities is non-cash and swings with SoundHound's share price; the company's non-GAAP figures exclude it (non-GAAP net loss $21.2M also excludes stock pay and other items).
SoundHound closed its acquisition of LivePerson on September 4, 2026, so Q3 includes less than a month of LivePerson's results plus deal-related costs in general and administrative expenses.
footerNote: SoundHound reports in thousands; figures here are exact to the thousand, shown in $M. SoundHound files its income statement with cost of revenue inside operating expenses; the chart shows it as the direct-cost step so the gross profit line ($21.3M, as the company itself reports) reads the same way as on every other page.
